sections.label: Uniform coin legal tender limits
sections.summary: The Bill sets a uniform legal tender limit of 20 coins per denomination in a single payment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill will, therefore, streamline the legal tender limits for coins to a uniform limit of 20 coins per denomination in a single payment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This means that a payer can use up to 20 pieces each of 5-cent, 10-cent, 20-cent, 50-cent and $1 coins per transaction.

sections.label: Currency Act amendments and coin limits
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Currency Act on IBNS-damaged notes, exempts certain licence holders, and lowers the 5-cent coin limit to 20.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill will amend section 23 of the Currency Act to make clear that an IBNS-damaged note is not legal tender.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Under specific conditions, the Bill will exempt a holder or applicant of a security service provider licence from the offence of mutilation of currency notes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, one of the key provisions in this Bill is to streamline the existing legal tender limits for coins to a uniform limit of 20 coins per denomination in each payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, for 5-cent coins, the number is brought down from 40 coins to 20 coins.

sections.label: DBS coin deposit fee
sections.summary: A check on DBS Bank's website showed a coin deposit fee of 1.5 cents per coin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A quick check on the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) Bank’s website indicated that the coin deposit fee is 1.5 cents per coin, which is a whopping 30% of the face value of a 5-cent coin.

sections.label: Minting cost and deposit fee funding
sections.summary: The speaker asks the estimated minting cost of each 5-cent coin and whether MAS should fund the coin deposit fee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On a slightly separate note, I would also like to ask what the estimated cost of minting each 5-cent coin is and whether it would make sense for MAS to fund the coin deposit fee to encourage the recirculation of 5-cent coins so that MAS does not have to mint new 5-cent coins.

sections.label: Limit on one-dollar coins
sections.summary: The amendment limits payment to 20 coins of the same denomination and introduces a limit on one-dollar coins.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the amendment, a person making payment can only insist on using a maximum of 20 coins of the same denomination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is probably most significant about the change is that it introduces a limit on the use of one-dollar coins, which did not exist before.

sections.label: IBNS for cash-in-transit security
sections.summary: The Bill legalises the use of IBNS as part of security systems protecting cash in transit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces provisions to legalise the use of IBNS as part of security systems to protect the movement of cash in transit (CIT).

sections.label: IBNS seller licensing amendments
sections.summary: The Bill amends the PSIA to require those intending to sell IBNS to obtain a licence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill also carries amendments to the PSIA to require those who intend to sell IBNS to obtain a licence to do so.

sections.label: Coin legal tender limits
sections.summary: The Currency Act is amended to set a limit of 20 coins across all denominations, with payor and payee able to agree otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, the Currency Act currently provides for a limit of $2 for 5-,10- and 20-cent coins, $10 for 50-cent coins and no limit for $1 coins, for legal tender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, we are amending the Act to provide for a limit of 20 coins to apply across all denominations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Of course, a payor and a payee can mutually agree to transact in any quantities of coins above the limit if they wish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe these amendments are reasonable and do not foresee any particular difficulties in their implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would, however, like to emphasise the broader and related point that in our drive towards a "cashless" society, we should take care to leave room for the co-existence of alternative payment methods, including physical currency, such as coins and banknotes, so that members of the public may have a choice in the payment methods they prefer.

sections.label: IBNS licensing and coin limits
sections.summary: Licensing IBNS for CIT operations frees Auxiliary Police Officers, and coin legal tender limits are revised to a uniform 20 pieces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the growing importance of shoring up security and defences against terrorism, we are always in need of support from the Singapore Police Force for a variety of security operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Therefore, the licensing of IBNS for CIT operations will help to free up Auxiliary Police Officers so that they can be deployed to do more important tasks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Therefore, in terms of financial impact, how costly will the use of such systems be for the banks?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These amendments also call for the revision of the legal tender limits for coins to a uniform limit of 20 pieces across denominations, which makes it easier for all to remember and implement it.

sections.label: New coin legal tender limit
sections.summary: The new legal tender limit allows a payer to use up to 100 coins, or $37 in total value, in a single transaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What this means is that the new legal tender limit for coins allows a payer to use up to 100 coins across the five denominations, or $37 in total value, in a single transaction.

sections.label: Cost of depositing coins
sections.summary: Depositing one coin currently costs $0.015, which can add up for large amounts of coins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Currently, it costs $0.015 to deposit one coin, and this can add up to a significant amount for large amounts of coins.

sections.label: Uniform 20-coin limit
sections.summary: The new uniform legal tender limit of 20 coins applies to each of the five denominations, allowing up to 100 coins or $37.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The new uniform legal tender limit of 20 coins applies to each of the five coin denominations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Thus, it allows a payer to use up to 100 coins, or $37 in total value, in a single payment transaction.

sections.label: Reduction for $1 coins
sections.summary: The main reduction applies to $1 coins, from no limit to 20 coins, or $20.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The main reduction is really for $1 coins, as Ms Sylvia Lim had pointed out, from no limit to 20 coins, or $20.

sections.label: MAS e-payment initiatives and cash
sections.summary: MAS has implemented e-payment initiatives like FAST, PayNow and SGQR, while ensuring cash remains an option for those used to it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Over the last couple of years, MAS has implemented many initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I mentioned in the last Bill debate, from Fast and Secure Transfers (FAST), PayNow, Singapore Quick Response (SGQR) code, all these make e-payments a lot easier to use so that people are naturally attracted to use e-payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And while we do that, always ensure there is the option of still using cash because, as Mr Chen Show Mao pointed out, there will still be members of our society who are still very used to using cash.

sections.label: Engagement on IBNS cash transport
sections.summary: MHA and MAS have been engaging the Association of Banks in Singapore on the use of IBNS for cash transport services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MHA and MAS have been engaging the Association of Banks in Singapore on the use of IBNS for cash transport services.
